pinyin: bù pà yī wàn, jiù pà wàn yī
gloss: Not afraid of ten thousand, just afraid of one in ten thousand.
teaser: Today, we're tackling a phrase that reminds us to prepare for the unexpected.
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Today, we're tackling a phrase that reminds us to prepare for the unexpected. [break 1s] The phrase is: 不怕一万，就怕万一 (bù pà yī wàn, jiù pà wàn yī). [break 1s] 不 (bù) - not [break 0.5s] 怕 (pà) - afraid [break 0.5s] 一万 (yī wàn) - ten thousand [break 0.5s] ，(,) - comma [break 0.5s] 就 (jiù) - just [break 0.5s] 怕 (pà) - afraid [break 0.5s] 万一 (wàn yī) - one in ten thousand [break 1s] So, the full idiom is 不怕一万，就怕万一, which literally means 'not afraid of ten thousand, just afraid of one in ten thousand,' and figuratively suggests that we should be cautious about unlikely but possible risks. [break 1s] Here’s the story behind it: [break 1.5s] This idiom originated from a time when people faced unpredictable challenges. It emphasizes the importance of being prepared for unexpected situations, even when they seem rare. Over time, it has become a reminder that caution in the face of uncertainty is wise. [break 1.5s] Now, let’s look at some examples: [break 1s] 在做任何投资之前，不怕一万，就怕万一。 [break 1s] Before making any investment, don’t be afraid of the large numbers, just be cautious about the unlikely risks. [break 1s] 虽然计划很完美，但不怕一万，就怕万一。 [break 1s] Although the plan is perfect, we should be cautious about the unlikely problems. [break 1s] 上课时，不怕一万，就怕万一，要准备好所有材料。 [break 1s] During class, don’t fear the many topics, just be ready for the unexpected questions. [break 1s] So, today’s idiom is 不怕一万，就怕万一, reminding us to be careful of the unlikely possibilities. Thank you for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom. [break 1s]
